insights: This slug duplicates work already merged under sibling cauchy-interlacing-theorem-oq-01-oq-02 (#28084). The Rayleigh-agreement hypothesis of the abstract poincare_separation is discharged by rayleigh_compress_eq, which is stated for an ARBITRARY submodule H (nothing uses codim=1), so the abstract theorem and the explicit compression join for any codimension m with no new work.

Rayleigh discharge mechanism: for y∈H, ⟨compress T H y, y⟩_H = ⟨P_H(Ty), y⟩ = ⟨Ty, y⟩_V by the orthogonal-projection adjoint identity (P_H self-adjoint, P_H y = y); norms agree since the inclusion H↪V is a linear isometry.

The interlacing μ_k ≤ λ_k is an equality on a block exactly when the corresponding invariant subspace is T-stable. compress T H loses information only through the orthogonal projection P_H(T ↑y); when T ↑y already lies in H the projection is the identity, so compress collapses to the restriction and no eigenvalue is lost — the extremal case of Poincaré separation.

Converse of the compression-attainment picture: the compression's projection error vanishes on y∈H precisely when H is invariant; a lifting S exists iff the ambient image T↑y lands back in H (read off from Submodule.coe_mem of compress T H y).

Attainment/spectrum-inclusion case of Cauchy interlacing: on invariant H the compression = T.restrict (compress_eq_restrict_of_invariant), so its whole spectrum {μ_k} ⊆ spec(T) and the bound μ_k ≤ λ_k degenerates onto the ambient spectrum. The pointwise eigenvalue-inclusion is the natural companion to the already-merged operator identity.

The attainment-case eigenvalue inclusion needs NO symmetry of T: invariance alone makes the orthogonal projection in `compress T H` inert on T↑v (coe_compress_of_invariant), so any compression-eigenvector v:H lifts to an ambient T-eigenvector ↑v∈V for the same μ. This generalises hasEigenvalue_compress_eigenvalue_of_invariant (which was stated for the symmetric descending-eigenvalue basis) to an ARBITRARY eigenvalue of the compression as an operator on H.

The one-sided inclusion spectrum(compress T H) ⊆ spectrum(T) sharpens to a full EQUALITY spectrum(T) = spectrum(compress T H) ∪ spectrum(compress T Hᗮ) exactly when H REDUCES T (both H and Hᗮ are T-invariant). This is the block-diagonal spectral decomposition and the two-block attainment case of Poincaré separation.

Symmetry-free reducing mechanism: the two projections P_H v and P_Hᗮ v of a T-eigenvector v are THEMSELVES eigenvectors of T for the same μ. Proof needs no adjoint/symmetry — only that T a - μ•a lands in H while the equal quantity μ•(v-a) - T(v-a) lands in Hᗮ, and H⊓Hᗮ=⊥ (Submodule.inf_orthogonal_eq_bot) kills anything in both. Key Mathlib: starProjection_apply_mem, sub_starProjection_mem_orthogonal, sub_eq_sub_iff_add_eq_add, Module.End.hasEigenvalue_iff_mem_spectrum.

The reducing-pair spectrum union spectrum(T)=spectrum(compress T H)∪spectrum(compress T Hᗮ) refines to a MULTIPLICITY statement: each eigenspace splits as an internal orthogonal direct sum eigenspace(T,μ)=(eigenspace(T,μ)⊓H)⊕(eigenspace(T,μ)⊓Hᗮ), so dim eigenspace(T,μ)=dim(·⊓H)+dim(·⊓Hᗮ). The multiplicity of μ for T is the exact sum of its multiplicities on the two blocks — the eigenspace-level (not just set-level) form of block-diagonalisation. Symmetry-free.

The whole reducing-subspace theory is driven by one reusable mechanism (now factored as starProjection_eigenvector_of_reducing): if T v=μ•v and H reduces T, then P_H v and v-P_H v are THEMSELVES μ-eigenvectors. Proof: T(P_H v)-μ•P_H v ∈ H equals μ•(v-P_H v)-T(v-P_H v) ∈ Hᗮ, and H⊓Hᗮ=⊥. Disjointness of the two eigenspace blocks needs NO invariance — purely Submodule.inf_orthogonal_eq_bot.
nextSteps: Iterate to a finite orthogonal family of mutually reducing subspaces V=⊕ᵢHᵢ (each Hᵢ T-invariant): spectrum(T)=⋃ᵢ spectrum(compress T Hᵢ) and dim eigenspace(T,μ)=∑ᵢ dim(eigenspace(T,μ)⊓Hᵢ), the full block-diagonalisation. Likely needs an induction over the family / DirectSum.IsInternal bridge.

Bridge the eigenspace-block finrank to the COMPRESSION eigenspaces: dim(eigenspace(T,μ)⊓H)=dim(eigenspace(compress T H,μ)) via the linear isometry H↪V restricted to the invariant block (compress=restrict there), turning finrank_eigenspace_eq_add_of_reducing into a statement purely about the two compressions.

Upgrade the descending-eigenvalue tuples: with H T-invariant, show the μ_k of compress T H form a sub-multiset (with multiplicity) of the λ_i of T — combine finrank_eigenspace_eq_add_of_reducing with the eigenvalue-counting of hT.eigenvalues across distinct IsSymmetric witnesses.
